deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio p.5 of Riemann's fair-copy manuscript of the 1859 Monatsberichte paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse'. The text matches the printed paper almost word for word. The previous page has established three things: the Perron/Fourier inversion f(x) = (1/2πi)∫_{a-i∞}^{a+i∞} (log ζ(s)/s) x^s ds for a>1; its integrated-by-parts form f(x) = -(1/2πi)(1/log x)∫ d/ds[log ζ(s)/s] x^s ds; and the substitution log ζ(s) = (s/2)log π − log(s−1) − log Π(s/2) + Σ_α log(1+(s−1/2)²/α²) + log ξ(0). Here Π(s/2)=Γ(s/2+1) is expanded as a Weierstrass-type product. The (s/2)log π term contributes nothing, since (1/s)(s/2)log π is constant and its s-derivative vanishes. The log ξ(0) term was already evaluated on the previous page.

Step 1. Every remaining term has the form ±(1/2πi)(1/log x)∫_{a-i∞}^{a+i∞} d/ds[(1/s) log(1−s/β)] x^s ds. The values of β are:
- β=1, from −log(s−1), up to a constant;
- β=−2n, from the Π-product;
- β=ρ=1/2±iα, from the zero product, where (1+(s−1/2)²/α²) is proportional to (1−s/ρ)(1−s/ρ̄).

Step 2. Differentiate with respect to the parameter β: ∂/∂β[(1/s)log(1−s/β)] = (1/s)·(s/β²)/(1−s/β) = 1/((β−s)β).

Step 3. For Re s = a > Re β and x>1, close the contour to the left, picking up the residue at s=β. This gives −(1/2πi)∫ x^s ds/((β−s)β) = (1/β)(1/2πi)∫ x^s/(s−β) ds = x^β/β. This equals ∫_∞^x t^{β−1}dt when Re β<0, and ∫_0^x t^{β−1}dt when Re β>0.

Step 4. Integrate in β; the order of integration and differentiation is exchanged, which is my gloss. Partial integration in s turns the left side back into −(1/2πi)∫ (1/s)log(1−s/β) x^s ds. This equals ∫_∞^x t^{β−1}/log t dt + C in the first case and ∫_0^x t^{β−1}/log t dt + C in the second, since d/dβ of each right side is the integral of Step 3.

Step 5. Fixing the constants.
- First case: C is found by letting Re β → −∞, where both sides tend to 0, so C=0.
- Second case: ∫_0^x is many-valued. It differs by 2πi according as the path runs through complex values with positive or negative argument. Along the first path it tends to 0 when Im β → +∞; along the second, when Im β → −∞.
- The branch of log(1−s/β) on the left is chosen to match, so that the constant vanishes. This is the definition of Li(x^ρ) for complex ρ.

Step 6. Assembling the terms:
- β=1 gives +Li(x).
- Each zero ρ=1/2±iα gives −Li(x^ρ).
- β=−2n gives ∫_x^∞ t^{−2n−1}/log t dt, using Σ_{n≥1} t^{−2n−1} = 1/(t(t²−1)).
- The constant term gives log ξ(0).
The result is the explicit formula f(x) = Li(x) − Σ_α [Li(x^{1/2+iα}) + Li(x^{1/2−iα})] + ∫_x^∞ dt/((t²−1) t log t) + log ξ(0). The sum runs over α with positive real part, ordered by size.

Step 7. Convergence. Riemann claims that, with this ordering, the series Σ(Li(x^{1/2+αi})+Li(x^{1/2−αi}))·log x equals the limit as b→∞ of the symmetric truncated integral (1/2πi)∫_{a−bi}^{a+bi} d/ds[(1/s)Σ log(1+(s−1/2)²/α²)] x^s ds. He adds that a different arrangement could give any real value, i.e. the series is only conditionally convergent.

Step 8. Möbius inversion. From f(x) = Σ_n (1/n) F(x^{1/n}) he inverts to F(x) = Σ_m (−1)^{μ(m)} (1/m) f(x^{1/m}). Here m runs over squarefree integers and μ(m) is the number of prime factors of m. In modern notation this is F(x) = Σ μ(m)/m · f(x^{1/m}). The page ends with the start of the density discussion: truncate Σ^α and differentiate; this continues on the next page.
errors: The constant 'log ξ(0)' is wrong as it stands. With Riemann's ξ(t), s=1/2+it, ξ(0) is the value at s=1/2. The correct constant is log of the value at s=0 (t=i/2), i.e. log(1/2) = −log 2. The mismatch arises because Σ log(1+(s−1/2)²/α²) is normalized at s=1/2, whereas the terms log(1−s/ρ) used here are normalized at s=0. The renormalization constant is lost, as is also not handled for −log(s−1) vs −log(1−s). This is a known slip in the published paper, discussed by Edwards.

Interchanging the β-integration with the s-integral, and the passage from the convergent derivative form back to the non-absolutely convergent form −(1/2πi)∫(1/s)log(1−s/β)x^s ds, are stated without justification. These steps were made rigorous only by von Mangoldt (1895).

The claim that Σ_α Li(x^ρ), summed in order of increasing α, equals the limit of the symmetric truncated integral is asserted as 'leicht zu zeigen'. It in fact requires zero-counting estimates, N(T) ~ (T/2π)log(T/2π), and growth bounds on ξ. It was first proved by von Mangoldt in 1895.
The phrase 'positiven Wurzeln' presupposes real α, i.e. the Riemann hypothesis. Riemann hedges this with the parenthetical '(oder einen positiven reellen Theil enthaltenden)'.

results.what: Explicit formula f(x)=Li(x)−Σ_ρ Li(x^ρ)+∫_x^∞ dt/((t²−1)t log t)+const for the weighted prime-power count f(x)=Σ_n π(x^{1/n})/n
results.modern_name: Riemann's explicit formula (Riemann–von Mangoldt explicit formula)

results.what: Evaluation of each term via ∂/∂β of (1/s)log(1−s/β) and the residue x^β/β, with the branch of Li(x^β) fixed by the limit as Im β → ±∞
results.modern_name: Perron-type contour integral / definition of Li(x^ρ) by analytic continuation

results.what: Conditional convergence of the sum over zeros: correct value only when terms are ordered by |Im ρ|; by rearrangement any real value is attainable
results.modern_name: Symmetric summation over zeros (Riemann rearrangement theorem applied)

results.what: Inversion F(x)=Σ μ(m)/m f(x^{1/m}) from f(x)=Σ F(x^{1/n})/n

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the fair-copy manuscript of p.5 of Riemann's published 1859 prime-number paper, nearly verbatim. Every result on it is famous and already attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: The residue at s=β equals x^β/β, the value of −(1/2πi)∫x^s/((β−s)β)ds for x>1
∫_0^x t^{β−1}dt = x^β/β for Re β>0; should be 0
Σ_{n≥1} t^{−2n−1} = 1/(t(t²−1)) for t>1, the source of the integral term; should be 0
The completed ξ at s=0 equals 1/2, so the correct constant is log(1/2) = −log 2
Möbius inversion recovers F from f(x)=Σ F(x^{1/n})/n

transcription_corrections: Line 'Im ersten Falle ... den [-zweiten-] {+reellen+} Theil': the image shows 'zweiten' struck through and 'reellen' inserted above; the transcription is correct.
In the 'Man hat daher' formula, the struck-out symbol after the derivative is 'ds' (written 'ds' and cancelled), not 'dx'.
The last line reads 'so giebt der Derivirte' in the manuscript; the printed version has 'die Derivirte'. This is a minor variant, not a transcription error.
Folio number '18' in the right margin and page number '5' at top right are archival/pagination marks, not part of the text.
